researched_by: press coverage of the Authority's 10 June 2026 decision
policy_summary:
RESOLVED 10 June 2026. The Authority reversed the April restriction and will maintain 24-hour access at the vast majority of its car parks, pending a wider review.

The important part is their own wording: this 'does not represent a change in policy... overnight stays have never been permitted'. So the car parks being open 24 hours does NOT mean you may sleep in them. Two separate facts, and reading the reversal as permission would be wrong.

An ANPR pilot at Llyn Tegid and Llangywer remains under consideration. The Authority directs campervan and motorhome users to designated campsites.

sites.name: Betws-y-Coed long stay car park
sites.notes: Restricted 22:00-03:00 from 1 April 2026, reversed 10 June. 24-hour access restored - but overnight stays are still not permitted.

sites.name: Llyn Tegid car park, Bala
sites.notes: ANPR pilot still under consideration here and at Llangywer, after repeated concerns from Llangywer Community Council and Bala Town Council.

sites.name: All Eryri National Park Authority car parks
sites.notes: Overnight stays have never been permitted in ENPA car parks, whatever the opening hours. The Authority directs users to designated campsites.

notes: The volatility case study, now with an ending. Restricted 1 April 2026, reversed 10 June - ten weeks. Any per-spot prohibition dataset would have been wrong for most of that window in one direction or the other.
